Continuous, soft (≲ 3 MeV) fast sources come out on top: Birmingham and FRANZ (design current) need ~2.4 days, FRM II MEDAPP ~4 (reactor off), LANSCE WNR and NPI Řež ⁹Be(p,n) ~16–17, all from dedicated studies on a Geant4 soft-beam background. ILL PF1B, the best cold beam, needs ~620 days: the detector's rate limits, not the flux, stop it. How the numbers are made

X17 per day*

The quickest number a facility can be put on, not a reach:

X17/day = n/s on the capsule × ⟨P⟩ × X17/IPC × 86 400

  • The n_TOF capsule: 500 bar ³He, Ø2 cm × 8 cm, beam along its axis. Its face takes the facility's flux at the experiment position (π cm²), or the n/s into the capsule where that is what is known.
  • ⟨P⟩: IPC pairs per entering neutron, ENDF/B σ and Born α folded over the source spectrum. Cold and thermal neutrons are all absorbed: 4.8×10⁻¹¹ each. At 1 MeV it is ~3×10⁻⁸.
  • X17/IPC = 1.5×10⁻³ (ATOMKI ⁴He), assumed at every E_n. "In window" is the share made at E_n ≤ 2.75 MeV, where E* matches ATOMKI.
  • Every X17 counted. No acceptance, trigger, background, dead time or rate limit. "≲" and "≈" mark rows with no number of their own, bounded by the facility named in their detail; "est." marks a number that rests on a guessed input (yield, spectrum split, geometry).

Days to ATOMKI (the figure of merit)

Beam days until the 3σ reach on X17/IPC comes down to ATOMKI's ⁴He value, 1.5×10⁻³: big plastics, best beam throttle, statistics only (no systematic floor, no setup or beam-off time). It comes from a dedicated study where there is one, else from the survey's two scaled models: cold/thermal beams on the ILL PF1B Geant4 rate walls; fast beams re-weight the GANIL/NFS and soft-beam Geant4 event lists to each source's spectrum, intensity and time structure. The reach is background-dominated, so it falls as 1/√T and days = 50 × (ρ₅₀ / 1.5×10⁻³)².

2-week reach

The same reach quoted for a 14-day run, ρ₅₀ × √(50/14). The write-ups quote 50 days: one ILL reactor cycle, the unit the study began with. Days to ATOMKI needs no choice of run length.
